text:
sara: Quick note from magnet-onboard: I found a reproducible 'handshake lag' that drops ~6 tokens when streaming immediately after a ~62k prefill on quantized builds. Repro on two nodes.
tom: missing tokens or misranked?
sara: missing contiguous tokens at the tail; generator jumps forward. Happens reliably for int4 on our rigs, float32 clean, int8 flaky.
mei: which lengths? any shard correlation?
sara: observed when prefill length in [61400..64512] and often when (len % 1024) in the 512..1024 window. More common on shard 4.
tom: logs?
sara: pasted minimal log snippet: 
[2026-11-05T08:11:22Z] prefill done len=63488 shard=4 epoch=301 fp=0xabc1
[2026-11-05T08:11:22Z] transition -> stream_start
[2026-11-05T08:11:22Z] stream recv tokens 63480..63486
[2026-11-05T08:11:22Z] ERROR dropped tokens 63487..63492
[2026-11-05T08:11:22Z] resumed at 63493
mei: epoch/fp diff?
sara: pref_epoch=301 stream_epoch=302 pref_fp=0xabc1 stream_fp=0xabc1 (same fp, epoch bumped).
tom: epoch bump + identical fp -> buffer swap but same bytes. Likely index remap during host transition. Suspect async memcpy/compact ordering in int4 path.
mei: quick canary: try KV_PREFILL_EVENT=1 (record/wait event) or KV_PREFILL_BARRIER=1 (host sync).
sara: KV_PREFILL_EVENT=1 removed the drop in my runs; barrier also fixes but costs more.
tom: good narrow. Action: (1) add event-based sync in int4 prefill before stream_start behind runtime flag; (2) add runtime assert to log pref_epoch != stream_epoch; (3) add onboarding regtest that runs 5 loops over edge lengths for quantized models.
mei: I'll audit other async memcpy + fused kernels to ensure events are recorded on the right stream.
sara: opened INF-4120 with repro, logs and a small canary PR. devbot: Canary deploy queued 2026-11-05T12:00Z by sara.
tom: thanks. Keep perf numbers if event sync has measurable impact.
mei: if event sync is heavy we can switch to per-kernel event records instead of host barrier.
sara: noted. Updating model-onboard checklist: "long-prefill handshake racecheck (quant)". I'll post canary results here.
